threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Overground is just fancy for a train. Wait till you see rush hour on a Tuesday.
Last night on the 59, a guy sang a whole Adele song, and the bus clapped when he finished. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy playing the saxophone in the U-Bahn while a toddler danced around him, the whole carriage just smiled. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves vegan currywurst—I've seen locals debate it like it's a gourmet dish!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they instinctively avoid the BART platform on Fridays. No one who really lives here goes near that chaos when the brakes go out.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 in rush hour, packed as ever. If you listen closely, you can hear the bus driver's playlist through the loudspeakers—today was classic '90s hip-hop. Instant mood lift.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think our plaça is just for picnics. It’s actually our stage—every weekend, local bands play, and it’s packed with real-life conversations, not just selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with paella customs—ordering it for lunch like it's a regular dish, when locals save it for Sunday.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal for a pub to serve breakfast at 10am. Everyone knows it's brunch or nothing, mate.
Heard a guy on the 196 bragging about how he can smuggle a whole pizza into the club. No one batted an eye, just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last summer, I saw a guy on his balcony watering his plants while barbecuing sausages. Gotta love the multitasking spirit of Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Turkish bakery open at 3 AM serving fresh simit while the pink dawn breaks over the Spree. Pure magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they seamlessly navigate the BART delays; they don't panic, just pull out a book and settle in.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman in the Tenderloin serenading the bus stop crowd with her guitar, not a soul seemed to mind the delay. Just another day in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the park is just for picnicking. Most locals come for the dodgeball games and impromptu dance sessions after dark.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confused look when the tram goes past without stopping—still thinking it’s a bus.
